name: The shrinkage alarm flags misconfigured pooling
non_visual_rationale: An alarm row in the operator's file; by design nothing else anywhere reacts to it.
criteria_delivered: 1. src/learning/metrics.ts's shrinkage section already carried one row per gated spot with shrink_weight, n and reporters (05-01's shipped shape, unchanged); this step replaces flagged's deferred `false` literal with a real computation over the same row, read straight off the stored record's own fields.

2. shrinkageOf now calls isOverPooled(key.n, key.shrunk_from_global), a two-constant guardrail declared next to their citation (SHRINKAGE_ALARM_MIN_N = 80, SHRINKAGE_ALARM_MIN_WEIGHT = 0.6, both 09 section 17.4 guardrail 2). The AT's SHRUNK_SPOT (n=80, shrunk_from_global=0.6) is flagged true; its HEALTHY_SPOT control (n=80, shrunk_from_global=0.1) is flagged false. Both assertions pass at GREEN, in the same run.

3. The flag is an alarm only: shrinkageOf's signature and every caller are unchanged (buildMonthlyMetrics -> evaluate.ts -> the one metrics.json write), and no new consumer, store write, or branch reads shrinkage[].flagged anywhere in src/. The AT's own assertWritesConfinedToMetrics harness (shared by every slice-05 acceptance test) confirms the run still writes exactly one file, under learned/metrics/v1/ alone.
criteria_deferred: No softer/banded warning tier (e.g. a 'watch' state below the hard alarm) is built -- 09 section 17.4 guardrail 2 states a single binary threshold, and the AT fixture pins exactly two states (flagged / not flagged). A future step wanting a graduated alarm needs its own criterion and its own AT evidence.

No consumer of shrinkage[].flagged is wired anywhere (dashboard, alert, automated response) -- explicitly out of scope per adr-pooling-hierarchy-activation decision 6: the alarm is for a human to read, and building a consumer is a future, separately-justified step.
scope_note: files_to_modify named exactly src/learning/metrics.ts and tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts; both were touched and nothing else in src/ was. evaluate.ts, declarations.ts, cross-validation.ts, load-correction.ts, fit.ts, inputs.ts, build.ts, hierarchy.ts and shrink.ts (the explicit do-not-touch list) needed no edit and were not touched -- shrinkageOf already read shrunk_from_global straight off the stored StoredCorrection record built upstream by fit.ts/correction-file.ts, so the alarm needed no refit and no new plumbing, exactly as the design context states. Confirmed by the post-GREEN wiring check: git diff --name-only shows only metrics.ts changed under src/.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: Both guardrail comparisons are inclusive (n >= 80, shrink_weight >= 0.6), not strict. The AT pins the boundary itself as the flagged case (SHRUNK_SPOT: n=80, shrunk_from_global=0.6 -> flagged true), and 'eighty mornings still sixty percent shrunk' reads as the boundary being the misconfiguration, not the open interval past it.

tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts's pre-existing shrinkage pass-through property (authored 05-01, asserting flagged: false unconditionally) was updated to compute its expected flag from an independently-restated threshold (SHRINKAGE_ALARM_MIN_N_ORACLE / SHRINKAGE_ALARM_MIN_WEIGHT_ORACLE, declared in the test file, not imported from metrics.ts's private constants) rather than left hardcoded false. This is the documented, expected consequence of the deferred literal this step's own job is to replace (metrics.ts's file header explicitly named this row as 05-05's to fix); the test's other assertions (spot_id/shrink_weight/n/reporters pass-through) are unchanged. No AT oracle was touched -- the only AT edit is the describe.skip removal.

The two new unit properties assert TRUE IMPLICATION monotonicity (flagged(low) implies flagged(high)) across the full generated domain, not merely 'stays flagged once already above threshold' -- this also exercises the boundary-crossing transition from unflagged to flagged, which a narrower 'starts already flagged' property would have missed.

The DESIGN_CONTEXT's third candidate law (a row's flag depends only on its own record fields, unaffected by other spots in the same run) was not authored as a separate property: the AT's own fixture already exercises two independent spots (SHRUNK_SPOT and HEALTHY_SPOT) in one run and asserts each independently, and shrinkageOf's implementation is a plain per-item .map over corrections with no cross-item aggregation, so a dedicated permutation property would have added ceremony without meaningfully increasing detection power for a two-line pure map. Flagged if reviewer disagrees; can be added on request.
acceptance: a-spot-still-mostly-pooled-after-eighty-mornings-is-flagged.test.ts, pre-authored by DISTILL, describe.skip removed (the only touch made to the file). One scenario, two spots: playa-empozada (n=80, shrunk_from_global=0.6) must be flagged true; playa-venao (n=80, shrunk_from_global=0.1) must be flagged false; both rows must carry n=80 and reporters=12 read straight off the stored correction; and assertWritesConfinedToMetrics must show the run wrote exactly one new key, the month's metrics file, and nothing else changed anywhere in the store. Passes at GREEN; no oracle was edited.
unit_law: Two fast-check properties added to tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts, neither of which the AT's two fixed examples can prove alone: (1) flagged(n, weight) implies flagged(n, higherWeight) at a fixed n, generated over the full [0,1] shrink-weight domain and n in [10,300] -- the guardrail never turns a flagged row unflagged as pooling only deepens; (2) flagged(n, weight) implies flagged(higherN, weight) at a fixed shrink weight, generated over n in [10,300] -- the guardrail never turns a flagged row unflagged as evidence only grows. Both use a shared flaggedFor(n, weight) helper driving buildMonthlyMetrics with one applied key, i.e. through the pure function's own driving port. In addition, the pre-existing shrinkage pass-through property (05-01) was repaired (see design_decisions_not_stated_upstream) so its own generated n/shrink_weight combinations assert the correct flag rather than a stale false literal -- this is a fix to an existing test's oracle, not new authorship, and is not counted in the budget below.
test_budget: 2 distinct behaviors this step introduces: (a) the exact-value threshold judgment (n>=80 AND shrink_weight>=0.6 names the alarm, read off the AT's two pinned examples plus the repaired pass-through property's now-correct oracle across its generated domain); (b) the monotonicity invariant of that judgment (never turns off as either dimension only grows), which 09 section 17.4 guardrail 2's design context names as two separate candidate laws (monotone in weight at fixed n, monotone in n at fixed weight). Budget = 2 x 2 = 4. This step authored 2 new unit properties (one per monotonicity direction) and activated 1 pre-authored AT scenario (2 assertions inside it, covering behavior (a)'s two concrete instances). Total new+activated test count = 3, within budget; no consolidation pattern needed. The permutation-independence candidate law was deliberately not authored as a fourth test (see design_decisions_not_stated_upstream) to stay inside budget without losing meaningful coverage.

Semantic AssertionError: "eighty mornings still sixty percent pooled away is a misconfiguration -- tau wildly off, or a parent eating its children -- and the file must say so (09 s17.4 guardrail 2): {\"spot_id\":\"playa-empozada\",\"shrink_weight\":0.6,\"n\":80,\"reporters\":12,\"flagged\":false}" -- true !== false, on the deferred literal, not a collection/import error. Unit: after implementing GREEN, running the pre-existing tests/unit/learning-metrics.test.ts surfaced the expected consequence -- the 05-01 pass-through property's hardcoded `flagged: false` failed for the right reason ("the shrinkage row must read shrink_weight, n and reporters straight off the stored correction, never invent them", received flagged:true for a generated n=80/weight=0.6 case), which is what motivated repairing its oracle rather than the code.
falsifiability_evidence: Two mutations to src/learning/metrics.ts's isOverPooled, each planted, run, and reverted; revert confirmed clean via `git diff --stat src/learning/metrics.ts` (only the intended +20/-5 lines remained) and a full green re-run. (1) `return true` (always flag): re-ran the AT + unit file -> EXIT=1, 3 failed -- the AT's healthy-spot assertion (playa-venao must be flagged false), the repaired pass-through property (a generated low-n/low-weight case now wrongly flagged), and the runMonthlyEvaluationOnce store-driven example (n=50 case must stay flagged:false). The two new monotonicity properties stayed green under this mutation, as expected -- an always-true function is trivially monotone, so a monotonicity-only property cannot by itself catch an over-firing alarm; the exact-value tests are what catch it. (2) `return false` (never flag, the original deferred behaviour): re-ran -> EXIT=1, 2 failed -- the AT's over-pooled-spot assertion (playa-empozada must be flagged true) and the repaired pass-through property (a generated high-n/high-weight case now wrongly unflagged). The monotonicity properties again stayed green (vacuously true, as an always-false function is also trivially monotone) -- confirming by construction that the exact-value tests, not the monotonicity ones, are the falsifiability backstop for both directions of a wrong-constant mutation, while the monotonicity properties exist to catch a differently-shaped bug (e.g. a non-monotone threshold function) that the two fixed AT examples alone would not.
